solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A clue to some cut for tight-fitting garment?

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: the word costume, set swimming (jumbled), produces these two words

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about a cut of cloth for something snug to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer is itself the clue. 'Swimming' is an anagram signal and its letters rearranged give 'some cut'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathing suit is made to cling closely to the body, so it is a snug garment.

clue.text: Maybe Jewish house gets endless approval

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house

indicators.note: endless says the final letter of the word for approval is dropped

parts.note: a tick marks approval

explanation.surface: A Jewish household is supposedly given approval without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims TICK to TIC. 'Maybe' signals that Jewish is only one example of the wider term.
explanation.definitionFit: Semitic peoples include Jews and Arabs, so Jewish is an example of the broader category.

clue.text: Bits inside pub somewhere in NI

parts.note: an inn is a pub
the Ards is a peninsula and district in County Down, Northern Ireland (NI)

explanation.surface: Odd bits found inside a pub in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ards is an area in County Down, Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Guts or entrails are the bits found inside a body, the informal sense of the word.

clue.text: At one time in form spelt out a concept in applied mathematics

indicators.note: spelt out here means the letters of the preceding words are written out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone, at one point, wrote a mathematical idea out on a form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spelt out' rearranges all fifteen letters of 'At one time in form'.
explanation.definitionFit: This quantity measures a body's resistance to angular acceleration, a standard idea in mechanics.

clue.text: Number born, number at home being put up

indicators.note: in a down entry, being put up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: née means born, used before a maiden name
ten is a number
in means at home

explanation.surface: A figure is born, and another is housed at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being put up' reverses NEETENIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nineteen is a whole number, the one after eighteen.

clue.text: Box mostly used for storing a very short item of clothing

indicators.note: used for storing says the box holds the other pieces inside it
mostly means the last letter of the word for box goes

parts.note: a crate is a box
v is the short form of very

explanation.surface: A box is mostly used to keep a very small garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims CRATE to CRAT; 'used for storing' puts AV inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cravat is a neckcloth worn by men, an accessory you put on.

clue.text: Evidence showing one's handled drug? That brings rebuke

definitions.meaning: smack is heroin, so traces of it found on someone's arm would show they had handled it
a mild reprimand or token punishment

explanation.surface: Traces of a drug handled bring a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: Smack is slang for heroin; the literal reading pictures it on a wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a light punishment or reprimand, a token reproof.

clue.text: Consequences? They may get batsmen caught out

definitions.text: They may get batsmen caught out
definitions.meaning: in cricket, shots hit in the air rather than along the ground can be caught by a fielder

explanation.surface: Results of strokes that get cricket batsmen dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is out if a fielder catches the ball before it lands, so lofted strokes are risky.
explanation.definitionFit: Outcomes or results are what follow from an action.

clue.text: Carries on with old nurses

parts.note: ex means former, old
tends means nurses, looks after

explanation.surface: Someone continues working alongside former nurses.
explanation.definitionFit: To continue or prolong something is to make it last longer.

clue.text: Sun-follower, old fellow, one having a fixation

parts.note: Monday, abbreviated Mon, follows Sunday
a man is a fellow
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An old chap who follows the sun is someone obsessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' is Sunday, not the star: the day after is Mon.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an obsessive preoccupation with a single subject or idea.

clue.text: Back old-fashioned investment as something useful

indicators.note: Back at the front of the clue means the investment's name is read in reverse

parts.note: a TESSA was a Tax-Exempt Special Savings Account, a UK savings scheme withdrawn in 1999

explanation.surface: Supporting a dated investment as something worthwhile.
explanation.walkthrough: TESSA was a British tax-free savings account of the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: A valuable quality or resource is something that helps you.

clue.text: Italian community giving performance outside Italy

indicators.note: outside says the performance word goes round the letter for Italy

parts.note: a turn is a performance, an act on stage
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An Italian town puts on a show abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a city in northern Italy, capital of Piedmont.

clue.text: Manage to discover path from the peak

parts.note: a track is a path
coming down means descending from the top

explanation.surface: Find a route leading down from the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something after a search is to succeed in locating it.

clue.text: Orderly systems function when backed by people's leader

indicators.note: backed by means the function is followed, supported from behind, by the leader

parts.note: cos is the abbreviation for cosine, a trigonometric function
Moses led the Israelites out of Egypt

explanation.surface: A function works when it has the backing of a popular leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmos is an ordered, harmonious universe, the opposite of chaos.

clue.text: Good little girl accumulates no special knowledge allegedly

indicators.note: accumulates means the good little girl takes the word no inside

parts.note: sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: A well-behaved child gathers up a refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good little girl' reads as one phrase, but it splits into two pieces that wrap round the refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnosis is claimed esoteric spiritual insight, so 'allegedly' fairly signals that the knowledge is supposed.

clue.text: Sheepish male turning up, serious old nobleman

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the male sheep is read upwards

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
grave means serious

explanation.surface: A timid man arrives, followed by a solemn old aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepish' looks like 'shy', but means 'of sheep'.
explanation.definitionFit: A margrave was a German nobleman ruling a border province, a historical title.

clue.text: Saints in defeat? Such may resist change

indicators.note: in says the saints go inside the word for defeat

parts.note: to foil is to defeat
S is the abbreviation for saint, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A beaten Southampton side, nicknamed the Saints, refuses to adapt.
explanation.definitionFit: An old fogey who clings to outdated ways is called this, figuratively someone set in stone.

clue.text: As hot home supporter, turn up, excited to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with says the excited word comes first

parts.note: fired means excited, fired up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for turn is read upwards

parts.note: a go is a turn

explanation.surface: A heated home fan arrives, excited from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home supporter' suggests a football fan, but it is a stand in the hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: An andiron holds logs in a domestic fireplace, so it supports something hot.

clue.text: Puts down membership fee, payable now for collection

parts.note: a sub is a subscription
dues are charges owed and ready to be collected

explanation.surface: Pays a membership fee due for collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts down' suggests a deposit, but it means crushes.
explanation.definitionFit: To crush or suppress, for example a rebellion, is to bring it under control.

clue.text: Artificially produced man going beyond speed of sound

indicators.note: going beyond says the man comes after the speed

parts.note: Mach 1 (written Mach I) is the speed of sound
Ned is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone breaks the sound barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: Mach 1 is written with the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: Made by a mechanical process rather than by hand, so manufactured.

clue.text: Sea creatures suffering mutilation Tom somehow removed

indicators.note: suffering signals that the letters of mutilation are damaged and rearranged
somehow removed says the name Tom is taken out of the jumbled letters in any order

explanation.surface: Marine animals have been mutilated and their owner is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: MUTILATION minus T, O, M leaves UILATIN, rearranged into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: These are cephalopod molluscs with spiral chambered shells, living in the sea.

clue.text: Attractive girl heading student event? One may get into hot water

definitions.text: One may get into hot water

indicators.note: heading says the girl comes first

parts.note: a dish is an attractive person
rag is a British students' charity event

explanation.surface: A pretty girl leads a student event and lands in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot water' looks like trouble; it is the sink. RAG is a British student fundraising week.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth for washing up plates is dipped into hot water in the sink.

clue.text: Maybe local journalist in East Anglia is treated badly

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, East Anglia
ED is short for editor, perhaps of a local paper

explanation.surface: A local newspaperman in East Anglia gets harsh treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: Diss is a small town in Norfolk, in the east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang 'diss' means to disrespect, so the past form means disparaged.

clue.text: Talking audibly and grooving

indicators.note: audibly says the word for talking is heard, not seen

parts.note: rabbiting (on) is British slang for chattering at length

explanation.surface: Someone chatting loudly while enjoying music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grooving' suggests dancing; in carpentry it is cutting a slot.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbet is a recess cut along a board's edge, so cutting one is making a channel in wood.

clue.text: Such cries may be heard in fortifications

indicators.note: may be heard says the word for fortifications is spoken

parts.note: walls are defences, fortifications

explanation.surface: Shouts echo around castle defences.
explanation.definitionFit: Wauls are howls or wails, as of a cat, so they are a kind of cry.

clue.text: Old Penny, woman offering advice when there's scare

parts.note: D was the abbreviation for a penny in pre-decimal British money
an agony aunt gives advice in a magazine column

explanation.surface: An elderly woman named Penny counsels someone frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Penny' looks like a name; it is the pre-1971 British penny, written d.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimidate or discourage someone is to frighten them.

clue.text: One who criticises what lawn specialist uses

definitions.meaning: to scarify is to criticise severely, so this is a harsh critic
a tool or machine that rakes out thatch and moss from turf

explanation.surface: A critic and a gardener's tool share a name.
explanation.definitionFit: One meaning is a harsh critic; the other is a raking machine for turf.

clue.text: Organised gang discredits a president of yesteryear

indicators.note: Organised says the letters of the following words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A criminal gang ruins the reputation of a former head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' rearranges GANG DISCREDITS A.
explanation.definitionFit: Valéry Giscard d'Estaing was President of France from 1974 to 1981.
